case_studies.title: MemPilot: Orchestrating On-Demand Multimodal Memory Curation for LLM Agents
case_studies.abstract: Memory has become integral to the LLM agent ecosystem, supporting information retention and reuse across interactions. However, most existing agent memory systems construct memory in a query-agnostic manner, which can incur unnecessary preprocessing cost and discard details that later prove essential. Recent studies have begun shifting memory processing toward runtime adaptation, but typically specialize in particular operations or fixed processing schemes, leaving flexible control over performance, cost, and latency largely underexplored. To address this challenge, we present \textbf{MemPilot
case_studies.summary: MemPilot addresses the waste of pre‑processing all memory data for LLM agents by introducing a runtime‑adaptive, multimodal memory curation system that lets you control performance, cost and latency on demand. The authors built a flexible orchestrator that curates only what is needed when it is needed, reducing unnecessary compute and storage usage. The result is a more efficient, cost‑aware memory pipeline for LLM applications.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage LLM services on cloud, 1) replace static memory pre‑processing with an on‑demand curator, 2) monitor cost and latency metrics to adjust thresholds, 3) tune the system to load only critical multimodal data when a query arrives.

case_studies.title: Beyond Semantic Similarity: Performance and Costs of Agentic Retrieval for Complex Tasks
case_studies.abstract: Modern information systems, including many agentic workflows, use dense retrieval to explore large amounts of unstructured data. However, dense retrieval relies on surface-level semantic similarity, which is insufficient for increasingly complex search applications. Here, we investigate agentic retrieval that combines the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) with the efficient corpus exploration of retrievers in a ReAct agentic loop to solve complex retrieval tasks. In our experiments, we show that agentic retrieval is more effective than standard retrieval, improving nDCG@10
case_studies.summary: The study shows that combining Large Language Models with dense retrieval in a ReAct agentic loop improves retrieval quality for complex tasks, achieving higher nDCG@10 scores than standard semantic similarity methods. It builds an agentic retrieval system that actively queries and refines results, demonstrating better performance on intricate information needs. This research directly affects cloud infra managers by offering a more precise retrieval approach that could be integrated into search services or knowledge bases.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud‑based search or knowledge‑base services, implement an agentic retrieval layer: 1) deploy an LLM that can generate follow‑up queries; 2) hook it into your existing dense retriever via a ReAct loop; 3) monitor nDCG@10 to validate performance gains.

It has moderate relevance to LLM API usage and agentic workflows, but does not provide immediate actionable insights for deployment, security, or cloud management.
